grh_1ae4b70a5b6055c8679a.title: Steve Charlotte Story
paragraphs: After receiving national praise for one of her poems, Charlotte Dixon decides that ordinary life in Rivers End and marriage to dependable Steve are stifling her artistic future. She plans to divorce him and go to the city for a literary career, insisting that she no longer loves the commonplace husband she once chose. Dr. Christian sees that Charlotte is romanticizing freedom, so he recruits sophisticated Barbara Powell to make a convincing show of being interested in Steve. At the town picnic Charlotte's confidence in leaving evaporates as she watches Steve apparently fall for another woman. When she abandons the divorce and demands another chance, Steve carries the charade far enough to make her face what losing him would mean, then admits he loves only Charlotte. Dr. Christian reveals that Barbara's romance with Steve was arranged to give Charlotte something more real than poetry to think about.

grh_1ab689f9b678920cd0c2.title: Simone
paragraphs: Fifteen-year-old Simone lives with her prosperous uncle as France collapses before the German advance. She discovers that he has hoarded gasoline, profiteered from refugees and intends to preserve his garage and vehicles for the occupiers rather than destroy them. Inspired by the example of Joan of Arc and by Maurice's warnings about collaboration, Simone steals the garage key and burns the entire property so the Germans cannot use it. Her uncle and local collaborators then try to force her to sign a false nonpolitical confession, but she refuses and is sent away still openly defiant.
